display.purpose: Hero name only, 5em (4em mobile), Lato 700, margins zeroed.

headline.purpose: Section titles (Expertise, History, Projects, Contact), browser-default h1.

title.purpose: Timeline card titles and skill card h3 headings.

lede.purpose: Hero role line (1.5em) and contact intro (1.2em).

body.purpose: All UI prose at an enlarged 1.1rem root size.

label-mono.purpose: Chips, timeline dates, GitHub/LinkedIn handles — machine-readable strings only.

shadows.name: card-rest
shadows.purpose: MDC elevation on white cards (timeline, contact items, contact buttons); constant, does not change on hover.

shadows.name: navbar-scrolled
shadows.purpose: Appears on the sticky navbar once the page scrolls.

shadows.name: drawer-edge
shadows.purpose: Left edge of the open mobile navigation drawer.

shadows.name: dot-cutout-ring
shadows.purpose: Ground-colored ring on 44px timeline dots so the spine passes behind them.

motion.name: state-transition
motion.value: color 0.15s ease-in-out, background-color 0.15s ease-in-out, border-color 0.15s ease-in-out
motion.purpose: The single transition used for all hover/state changes.

motion.name: app-fade-in
motion.value: app-fade-in 700ms ease-out both (opacity 0 to 1, translateY 20px to none)
motion.purpose: One-time app-level entrance on load, wrapping all sections.

motion.name: reveal-card
motion.value: opacity 0.4s ease-in, transform 0.55s cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.8, 0.25, 1) from translateY(24px)
motion.purpose: Timeline card scroll reveal; hidden state gated behind the JS-added .vt-reveal class so SSR/no-JS always sees cards.

motion.name: reveal-dot-bounce
motion.purpose: Timeline dot overshoot bounce on scroll reveal.

motion.name: reduced-motion-clamp
motion.purpose: Global prefers-reduced-motion clamp; scroll-behavior reverts to auto and reveal transitions are removed.

narrative.overview:
This system is a user-pinned faithful port of Yuji Sato's react-portfolio-template (MIT) into Angular 19. The world is a near-black developer portfolio: deep blue-black ground, white text, one electric violet accent, white cards floating on the darkness, and a single fixed-attachment hero image. Every value here is taken from the shipped code, not from the template's intent — where the build departs from the reference, the departure is a recorded user decision (the contact form became direct links) and the build wins.

The character is restrained and terminal-adjacent: Lato carries all UI prose at a generous 1.1rem body size, while Courier Prime marks machine-readable strings (tech chips, timeline dates, GitHub handles) the way a code editor marks literals. Depth is real but quiet — Material-elevation card shadows at rest, no gradients, no glass. Motion exists in exactly two places: a one-time 700ms app fade-in and the alternating timeline's scroll reveal, both disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.

Theme is a body-level class swap (light-mode on body, deep-linkable via ?theme=light): every ground, text, and muted token re-points; the accent and the entire white card system stay identical in both modes.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black ground (#0d1116) with white text; light mode swaps the ground to #f8f9fa and text to #0d1116, nothing else
One accent for both modes (#5000ca) used only as fills, dots, focus rings, selection, and the scrollbar — never as body text or large surfaces
White cards and white chips with card-ink text (rgb(39, 40, 34)) in both themes
Lato for all UI text; Courier Prime reserved for chips, dates, and handle strings
Two motion moments only (app fade-in, timeline reveal), both SSR-safe and reduced-motion-safe

rules.name: The One Violet Rule
rules.body: #5000ca is the only accent hue in either theme. It appears as small fills, markers, and interaction states — never as a large resting surface, never as decorative gradient, never as a second accent alongside anything else.

rules.name: The Card Stays White Rule
rules.body: Cards and chips keep white surfaces and card-ink text in dark and light mode alike. Theme changes touch grounds, text, and muted tones only; the card system is theme-invariant.

rules.name: The Mono Is Metadata Rule
rules.body: Courier Prime appears only on machine-readable strings — tech-stack chips, date ranges, GitHub/LinkedIn handles. UI prose is always Lato; mono is never used for headings, sentences, or buttons.

rules.name: The Shadow At Rest Rule
rules.body: Elevation is a property of the surface, not the state: cards carry Card Rest at all times, hover swaps the background to accent instead of lifting. Never add hover shadows or scale-on-hover to cards.

dos: Do keep all themeable values on the CSS custom properties (--bg, --text, --muted, --accent, --accent-text, --card, --card-text, --home-bg) so the light-mode class swap stays a one-place change.
Do use #5000ca for hover fills, dots, focus-visible rings (2px solid, offset 2px), selection, and the scrollbar — the complete list of its appearances.
Do keep state transitions at 0.15s ease-in-out (color, background-color, border-color) — the single transition speed the whole site uses.
Do gate any scroll-reveal hidden state behind a JS-added class (as .vt-reveal does) so SSR prerenders and no-JS visitors see full content.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion: reduce wherever motion is added — the global clamp already exists in styles.scss.
donts: Don't introduce a second accent hue, a gradient, or a colored large surface; the palette is grounds + white + one violet.
Don't use Courier Prime for headings, sentences, or buttons; mono is for chips, dates, and handle strings only.
Don't tint cards or chips with the theme; they are white with card-ink text in both modes.
Don't add fonts beyond Lato and Courier Prime (loaded weights: Lato 300/400/700/900 + italic 400, Courier Prime 400/700).
Don't add entry animation beyond the two shipped moments (app fade-in 700ms, timeline reveal); never animate on scroll elsewhere.
Don't give hover fills to non-actionable rows; static contact rows keep their white surface (the .static variant).
